request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: Rent shall be paid by pre-authorized debit from the Tenant's bank account on the first day of each month.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
Under the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006*, a landlord cannot require a tenant or prospective tenant to provide post-dated cheques or engage in automatic debiting of an account (such as pre-authorized debit) for the payment of rent. While a tenant and landlord can mutually and voluntarily agree to use automatic debit as a payment method, a mandatory lease clause requiring it is contrary to section 108 of the Act and is therefore void under section 4.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 108
